focus: Session handoffs and scene clip agency

route_status.proven_scope: The exact Godot 4.7.2 scripted story-clip probe passed: all 13 manifest clips were present, the real OGV started, Back and double-tap exits restored pause state, transformation queued before the epilogue/Day Two card, and clip-seen save state persisted (runtime/L53/attempt_1/probe.log: RESULT: PASS failures=0).
route_status.route_gaps: This probe calls the boss-defeated and Day Two hooks directly after assigning Day One state (scripts/probe_day_one_story_clips.gd:119-137); it does not reach these moments through a visible child-played route. Playback is headless with a synthetic clock/input fixture, so no Mobile image, actual finger timing, audio, device, or child experience is proven.

code_constants.value: Double-tap interval <= 450 ms; each tap held <= 350 ms; <= 24 px movement; taps within 80 px.
code_constants.scope: Code thresholds; runtime fixture uses a deterministic synthetic millisecond clock, not a child or device measurement.

code_constants.value: Playback timeout = manifest duration + 8 seconds (minimum 1 second plus margin).
code_constants.scope: Fallback timer code; normal end uses VideoStreamPlayer.finished. No gameplay session duration is established.

timing.assumptions: Probe process-frame waits are test synchronization, not child-facing clip duration. The helper wall time is not gameplay time.

tactile.target_size: The video fills a 16:9 aspect-fit area inside a full-screen overlay (scripts/day_one_story_clips.gd:84-107); there is no visible skip target to measure. Back is the alternate route. Physical target size on the Lenovo Tab M11 is unmeasured.
tactile.press_response: One tap is consumed by the movie; a second short tap meeting the 450 ms/80 px limits skips on release. The helper verifies the completion callback once and pause restoration, not rendered response latency (scripts/day_one_story_clips.gd:176-197; story_movie_skip_cases.gd:25-34).
tactile.drag_hold_release: A hold over 350 ms, drag over 24 px, canceled touch, or two simultaneous contacts invalidate the tap pair; the fixture checks each case (story_movie_skip_cases.gd:48-85).
tactile.ownership: Input tracks a single contact and resets the pending pair when multiple contacts are present; device-emulated mouse events are discarded to avoid counting Android touch twice (scripts/day_one_story_clips.gd:132-168). Synthetic fixture only; real touch ownership is unmeasured.
tactile.cancellation: Focus-out/background suspends playback and timer and clears pending taps; focus-in/resume starts a fresh pair (scripts/day_one_story_clips.gd:204-221; story_movie_skip_cases.gd:88-108). Back calls skip through the navigation stack (scripts/main.gd:6791-6798).

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: a self-paced double-tap or persistent Back route lets a child move through between-scene story beats when ready, while a single accidental tap does not cut the story short. No child tested that choice.
play_appeal.variety: The manifest and hook map span opening, room arrivals/completions, rescue, rainbow route, boss arrival/transformation, and epilogue (scripts/probe_day_one_story_clips.gd:15-39). The probe confirms wiring, not felt variety.
play_appeal.world_response: The clip overlay covers the castle and its voice caption; completion, skip, or cancellation restores covered layers (scripts/main.gd:6799-6812,6816-6835). Probe checks the handoff path, but no rendered transition was reviewed.
play_appeal.replay: A clip is marked seen and queued for save immediately after successful setup; the same save will not replay it (scripts/main.gd:6783-6801). This supports once-only continuity, though an interruption just after start may consume the clip; child tolerance for that outcome is untested.

play_sequence.inputs: One short tap, 451 ms pause, one short tap at the same point.
play_sequence.grounding: The fixture advances the synthetic clock by DOUBLE_TAP_MS + 1 and asserts no skip: tools/tests/fixtures/story_movie_skip_cases.gd:35-40.

play_sequence.grounding: Distant taps do not skip in tools/tests/fixtures/story_movie_skip_cases.gd:42-46; Back is wired to preview.skip in scripts/main.gd:6791-6798.

play_sequence.grounding: Direct probe hook and transition assertions: scripts/probe_day_one_story_clips.gd:119-151; queued clip drain precedes transition: scripts/day_one_flow.gd:396-412. Visible gameplay route remains unproven here.

observations.title: Exact-build probe verifies the clip lifecycle and story queue
evidence: audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L53/attempt_1/probe.log: DAY_ONE_STORY_CLIPS|RESULT: PASS failures=0; all 13 clips present and real OGV startup, skip-once, save persistence, transformation-to-epilogue handoff assertions pass.
scripts/probe_day_one_story_clips.gd:108-160: exercises a standalone player, then directly calls boss and Day Two hooks and checks queued card order and save state.
observations.reproduction: Run the retained receipt command once; it completed with exit code 0 and no failure lines. The story boundary is injected in the probe, so this proves the tested lifecycle assertions, not the preceding gameplay route.
observations.child_impact: Ordered clips can connect room play and the transformation/epilogue without the Day Two card overtaking them; a child-visible route or comprehension is not established.
observations.proposed_repair: No runtime repair indicated by this probe. Keep the routed visual/device and child evidence separate from this scripted lifecycle pass.
observations.acceptance_test: On a fresh profile, reach the boss boundary through touch gameplay and capture transformation, queued epilogue, card handoff, and a save reload without direct state injection.

observations.title: Skip is intentionally a precise double-tap or Back action
evidence: scripts/day_one_story_clips.gd:12-16,176-197: 450 ms pair window, 350 ms maximum individual tap, 24 px motion tolerance, 80 px pair distance; one valid tap alone leaves playback running.
tools/tests/fixtures/story_movie_skip_cases.gd:25-85,110-124: checks one tap, emulated mouse, late/distant pair, hold, drag, multi-touch, cancellation and one-time completion.
observations.reproduction: Inspect the input handler and the shared fixture; the automated fixture passes under a synthetic clock. No physical touch was observed.
observations.child_impact: A clear Back control offers a conventional exit, while requiring two quick taps without an on-screen cue may be undiscoverable or too exact for some young children.
observations.proposed_repair: No change justified from source review alone; validate the existing Back affordance and the double-tap gesture with a child before considering an alternative.
observations.acceptance_test: On the target phone, verify a child can continue the clip after a stray tap and can discover one reliable skip route without adult instruction; record actual tap spacing and whether Back is found.

observations.title: The overlay has no in-video skip prompt
evidence: scripts/day_one_story_clips.gd:84-107 builds a black background, aspect-fit video, and player; no child-facing skip prompt/control is created in setup.
scripts/main.gd:6787-6798 places the story layer at 28 below game-wide Back at 29 and routes Back to skip; comments say taps on the clip are swallowed.
observations.reproduction: Code inspection only. The probe asserts Back is wired and the overlay stops input; it does not capture or assess its visible affordance.
observations.child_impact: A child who wants to leave a long clip may need to notice and understand the separate Back control; the double-tap route has no visible teaching cue in the clip overlay.
observations.proposed_repair: Keep the current interface until a phone/child observation establishes whether the existing Back cue is discoverable; do not infer a defect from headless source inspection alone.
observations.acceptance_test: Show the running clip to a child unfamiliar with the gesture and observe whether they can either wait comfortably or find Back to return, without prompting.

observations.title: Once-only persistence begins when playback starts
evidence: scripts/main.gd:6794-6801: after successful setup, marks movie_id seen and queues a save before waiting for the finished signal.
scripts/day_one_story_clips.gd:204-221 pauses playback while app focus is lost; it does not clear the seen flag or replay on resume.
observations.reproduction: Source trace; the probe verifies seen persistence and focus suspension separately, but does not kill the app mid-clip and reload.
observations.child_impact: An interruption after clip start can leave the child with the story marked seen even if they watched only part of it; whether this creates confusion or is acceptable is unknown.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair proposed absent a reproduced harmful interruption case; test mid-clip app exit and re-entry on the target phone.
observations.acceptance_test: Start a clip, background or terminate the app at a recorded point, reopen the same save, and observe whether the child can continue the route without a confusing missing story beat or lost progress.

strengths.claim: A single tap does not accidentally skip the story; the tested completion paths restore the prior pause state once.
The transformation and epilogue queue before the Day Two card, and the story clip covers the castle layer while active.
strengths.evidence: scripts/day_one_flow.gd:396-414; scripts/main.gd:6799-6812,6816-6835; scripted queue assertions in scripts/probe_day_one_story_clips.gd:119-151.

acceptance_gaps: No routed-input proof through actual room completion, boss defeat and Day Two handoff; the probe injects state/hooks directly.
No Mobile-rendered evidence of the full-screen clip, Back visibility, aspect-fit bars or return seam.
No Lenovo Tab M11 touch latency, target dimensions, playback performance, audio audibility or interruption/reload evidence.
No observed-child evidence for skip discoverability, clip comfort, comprehension, agency, replay or fun; no owner acceptance is established.
